clue.text: Actor at reading messing up all the parts

indicators.note: messing up all the parts says every letter of the words before it is jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A performer at a play-reading makes a hash of every role he is given.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is a performer who specialises in tragic roles on stage.

clue.text: Present both sides of drama in play

indicators.note: in says the picked letters sit inside the word for play

parts.note: to toy is to play idly

indicators.note: both sides of picks the first and last letters of the word drama

explanation.surface: A gift showing both faces of a stage show within a play.
explanation.definitionFit: The present means the current day, now, rather than the past or future.

clue.text: Almost joined member of mission

indicators.note: Almost says the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: attached means joined or fastened

explanation.surface: Someone nearly signed up as part of a mission.
explanation.definitionFit: An attache is a staff member of a diplomatic mission or embassy.

clue.text: Issue yours truly raised before a race

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, read bottom to top

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: A matter I personally brought up ahead of a running contest.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something that issues or flows out from a source.

clue.text: So central, it entered somehow between the ribs

indicators.note: entered somehow says the preceding letters went in by some unknown route, so they come out rearranged

explanation.surface: Something central got in, no one knows how, among the ribs.
explanation.definitionFit: Intercostal is the anatomical term for what lies in the spaces between ribs.

clue.text: The rest of the game

definitions.meaning: a card game, short for Napoleon, in which players bid tricks

explanation.surface: The remainder of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The rest' looks like 'the remainder'; it is a short sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A nap is a short rest, and nap is also the card game Napoleon.

clue.text: Penniless family put in the street

indicators.note: put in says one piece is placed inside the abbreviation for the street

parts.note: kin means family, one's relatives

explanation.surface: A family with no money is evicted onto the street.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is British slang for having no money at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Skint is informal British slang for broke, having no money.

clue.text: Go away with supervisor, initially, to study

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word supervisor

parts.note: to cram is to study hard in a hurry

explanation.surface: A student leaves with their tutor to do some swotting.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is a slangy order to clear off or leave quickly.

clue.text: Lack of vitality — but it has its moments

definitions.meaning: sluggishness, a lack of energy or will to act
in physics a body has a moment of this, its resistance to turning

explanation.surface: A dull spell, though not without its high points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has its moments' sounds like 'is sometimes good'; it is the moment of inertia in mechanics.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is sluggish inactivity, and in mechanics resistance to change of motion, measured as a moment.

clue.text: TUC ranted about being subjected to cuts

indicators.note: about means around and in a jumble, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: The trade unions raged over having their budget slashed.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is the Trades Union Congress, the British federation of trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: Truncated means shortened by having a part cut off.

clue.text: Take away pamphlet on the lower classes

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece written on another comes after it

parts.note: D and E are the lowest grades in the British social classification of occupations
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.surface: Someone removes a leaflet aimed at the working classes.
explanation.walkthrough: British market research grades households A, B, C1, C2, D and E, so D and E are the lower classes.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract is to take away from something's worth or merit.

clue.text: As usual, contracted rendezvous for recently arrived celebrity

parts.note: par means the normal level, as in par for the course

indicators.note: contracted says the word is shortened by losing its last letter

parts.note: a venue is a meeting place, a rendezvous

explanation.surface: As ever, a brief meeting is arranged for a newly famous star.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is an upstart, someone who has newly risen to wealth or fame without the polish to match.

clue.text: Reportedly why you seize a' spiky plant

indicators.note: Reportedly says the words beside it are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: spoken, these words give the letters Y, U, two Cs (seize as C's) and A

explanation.surface: A gardener asks, in hearsay, why you would grab hold of a prickly plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Seize is heard as C's, the plural of the letter C, giving the double C.
explanation.definitionFit: The yucca is a plant of the agave family with stiff, sword-like pointed leaves.

clue.text: Treatment needed to cure him, over a time?

definitions.text: Treatment needed to cure him, over a time?

indicators.note: Treatment here means handling or working over the letters that follow, reshaping them

explanation.surface: A doctor wonders whether a patient needs a course of therapy over some period.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange CUREHIM with A and T. The whole clue also describes a sufferer from rheumatism, someone who needs long treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheumatic is a person suffering from rheumatism, the sort of patient needing lengthy therapy.

clue.text: Bridge players enthused one partner in fundamental way

parts.note: E and S are East and South, two of the four players at bridge
sent means thrilled, carried away
I is the Roman numeral for one
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: Card players were basically delighted with one of their partners.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the players are named by compass points, North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Essentially means basically, at heart, in the most fundamental respect.

clue.text: Shrub found 'between Parisian houses

definitions.meaning: an aromatic evergreen herb-shrub with bitter leaves, also called herb of grace
the French word for street, the gap that runs between houses in Paris

explanation.surface: A bush is discovered growing between two homes in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Rue is both a bitter-leaved garden shrub and French for a street, the way between houses.

clue.text: In actual case, combative American detectives involved in major murder

indicators.note: case says the word for actual forms an outer shell round the other pieces

parts.note: real means actual
a GI is an American soldier
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: In a real case, a fighting Yank and police detectives get mixed up in a big killing.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Regicidal describes killing a king, a crime of the highest order.

clue.text: Not obeying rules of one head waiter, for example

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
nob is old slang for the head
a waiter is one kind of servant

explanation.surface: A head waiter flouts the house regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'head waiter' is one job title; the parse splits it into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inobservant fails to keep or heed rules, the opposite of being observant of them.

clue.text: Music extremely limited at heart

parts.note: a popular music style named in three words, whose middle word 'and' is cut at both ends to one letter

explanation.surface: A tune with very little feeling behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: The style is usually written with 'n' for 'and', its central word shrunk at both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock and roll is the 1950s style of popular music, here written with its contracted middle word.

clue.text: Drink containing rum with extra key ingredient

indicators.note: ingredient says the extra letter goes in as part of the mix
rum means odd or strange, so the word beside it is taken in a strange new order

parts.note: D is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: A cocktail with rum in it plus one essential extra component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like part of the drink but is the anagram signal: CONTAINING is rearranged, then the key D is added among its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A long drink of the spirit mixed with quinine-flavoured mixer, served with ice and lemon.

clue.text: Refusal to name Theophrastus as a paragon

parts.note: no is a refusal
George Eliot wrote Impressions of Theophrastus Such, giving his surname

explanation.surface: A rejected nomination for a Greek philosopher as a model of virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theophrastus' looks like the Greek philosopher, but it is George Eliot's narrator Theophrastus Such.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonsuch, or nonesuch, is a person or thing without equal, a paragon.

clue.text: Provided courses for US agent

definitions.meaning: gave meals to someone, served them food
American slang for an FBI officer

explanation.surface: Someone served dinners to an American government operative.
explanation.definitionFit: Fed is the past tense of feeding people meals, and also US slang for a federal agent.

clue.text: Irritate by saying it's a precision tool

parts.note: to fret is to vex or worry
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: Annoyance at hearing that something is an exact instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A fretsaw is a fine-bladed saw for cutting intricate shapes in wood.

clue.text: Women not comfortable on the high seas, so to speak

definitions.text: Women not comfortable on the high seas, so to speak

parts.words: Women not comfortable on the high seas, so to speak
parts.note: reads as seasick women sailors, but high seas is said for high Cs: low-voiced female singers who struggle with top notes

explanation.surface: Some women feel queasy when out on the open ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' flags the pun: high seas stands for high Cs, notes beyond the range of the lowest female voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Contralti are singers with the lowest female voice, who avoid the top of the soprano range.

clue.text: One put in place to take various measures?

definitions.meaning: a sovereign installed on the throne to govern
a graduated strip used to measure lengths

explanation.surface: An appointee installed to bring in a range of policies.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one appointee; split it, and each half names a different sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is both a governing sovereign and a graduated strip for measuring.

clue.text: Do people want to have them? Yes and' no

definitions.text: Do people want to have them? Yes and' no

parts.words: Do people want to have them? Yes and' no
parts.note: people in want are in lack, so they both have these (requirements) and do not have them (the things required)

explanation.surface: A question about whether folk desire something, answered with a shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'want' plays on two senses: to desire, and to be in want or lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs are requirements: the poor have plenty of them yet lack what would meet them.

clue.text: English artist's guide

definitions.meaning: to direct or pilot a course

explanation.surface: A British painter's handbook.
explanation.walkthrough: Philip Wilson Steer (1860 to 1942) was an English painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Steer was an English painter, and to steer is to guide.

clue.text: Fellow's capital in tax haven

definitions.meaning: a man's first name, so any chap might carry it
the chief town of the Isle of Man, a low-tax offshore territory

explanation.surface: A man keeps his money in an offshore account.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea, is a well-known tax haven.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas is a common man's name and the capital of the Isle of Man.

clue.text: Whole seen here, but only part heard

indicators.note: heard says the word for only part is taken by its sound

parts.note: some means only part of the whole, not all

explanation.surface: A whole can be seen in this place, yet just a portion can be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: Written, the word is the whole (a total); spoken, it sounds like 'some', only part.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is a total, the whole amount.

clue.text: Brief inspection of butcher's followed by another

indicators.note: followed by says the second piece comes straight after the first

parts.note: Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look
another look is a see, a further glance

explanation.surface: A quick check of the butcher's shop, then of the next shop along.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang gives 'butcher's' (butcher's hook) for a look.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-see is an informal quick look or survey.

clue.text: Composer contributing to composition of subtle harmony

indicators.note: contributing to composition of says the name is formed from part of the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A composer adds to a piece full of delicate harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Lehár was the Hungarian composer of The Merry Widow.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehar was an Austro-Hungarian composer famous for operettas.

clue.text: Hawthorn bark

definitions.meaning: a thorny shrub whose white blossom comes in spring
barque, a sailing ship; here the Pilgrim Fathers' ship

explanation.surface: The rough outer skin of a thorn tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' looks like tree bark beside a tree; it is a sailing vessel, the ship that carried the Pilgrim Fathers in 1620.
explanation.definitionFit: May blossom is hawthorn flower, and the Pilgrims' ship of 1620 was a bark of that name.
